task.title: Task assignments: convergent ownership for humans and agent fleets
task.description:
Task assignments: convergent, additive ownership signals for humans and agent fleets. (Design agreed 2026-08-13; reframed from the original claim/lease-lock model — a lock asks for the one thing this architecture resists, an assignment is the collection semantics it already does best. Workbook's audience: solo devs and small teams driving agents in parallel; assignments signal responsibility, never strongly block, always overrideable by addition.)

## Design

**Data model.** assign.add / assign.remove operations on the task — an ordinary convergent collection, like labels and dependencies. Concurrent assignments both survive (multi-assignment is the semantics, not a conflict: pairing and independent-spike workflows are legitimate working modes). No leases, no renewal, no expiry: "began work" is assignment + in-progress status, and staleness is displayed (assigned N days ago, no activity since), never enforced by a clock.

**Identity.** The principal is the asserted git identity (user.email), already stamped on every operation — no roster, no verification protocol (verification would import a central authority the tool deliberately lacks; wrong emails are visible noise, socially corrected). Agents act as their principal qualified by a free-form label: an assignment value like dylan@example.com/impl-1 — authority keys on the email, the label answers which agent holds it. The team registry is the set of actor emails in project history (offered as --to completions). Opt-in future hardening if ever needed: signed-commit verification on assignment ops. Within Workbook's trust model (push access = trusted), asserted identity is as strong as everything else.

**Removal rule — strict, enforced at two layers.** An assignment is removable ONLY by its assignee-principal (any agent of the same email — an orchestrator sweeps up after its own fleet, including crashed agents) or by the actor who created it (so a mistaken tag of a teammate is undoable by its author). Enforcement: (1) mutation boundary refuses a foreign remove, exit 5; (2) THE FOLD — Apply deterministically treats a foreign remove as a recorded no-op, making the rule durable data-model contract even against hand-crafted ops, replayable, no new conflict type. This strictness is what dissolves the claim-fight loop: two agents force-claiming the same task terminates instantly in the both-assigned state (a meaningful spike outcome) instead of ping-ponging removals. An unremovable legacy assignment (departed teammate) blocks nothing — assignment is additive.

**The claim behavior (verb-level, not storage-level).** Self-assigning runs fetch -> check -> append -> push synchronously. If the task is already assigned to someone else: warn, distinct exit code (so a fleet agent can pick another task), --force proceeds additively — it can never remove the existing assignment. If the push loses a race, reconcile replays, and the post-replay state shows the other assignment: same warning path on the rebased view.

**Surface (nouns ride the existing verbs, per the comments-story convention).** workbook update <id> --assign [self|email[/label]] [--force] / --unassign [self|email/label]; assignments in show and both boards (chips with principal short-form + label, staleness display); workbook next skips tasks assigned to others by default (--any to override) and gains next --claim: pick + self-assign + push in one synchronous stroke for agents. Exact flag shapes, envelope members, and board rendering settle at implementation-design time.

**Scope notes.** Depends on the shipped reconcile machinery (WB-01KYD72S4N6RB51NP2KKHGE7AD, done). New operation types: must carry the writer-format marker (WB-01KZYH9C0JRQX0N46JHZ929XC4) — this story ships after it. The original story's remote-CAS/lease/abandoned-claim-recovery machinery is deliberately dropped, not deferred: the reframe makes it unnecessary.

## Shipped (2026-08-15)

Three PRs, each through adversarial execution-verified review (records on the PRs):

- **PR #98 (core, two rounds).** assign.add/assign.remove as a convergent collection; the removal rule enforced at both layers — boundary refusal AND the fold treating a foreign remove as a recorded no-op (RemovableBy reads only history: pack actor vs recorded principal/creator), proven durable against hostile hand-crafted packs synced between clones (byte-identical checkpoints, no attribution theft, no privilege escalation through the creator branch). task.create refuses smuggled assignments (the marker-header trap closed pre-emptively). Projection schema 4 with task_assignments — proven load-bearing (without it, an ordinary rename through the projection erased both holders from shared history). Cap boundary-only. Review blocker was a scratchpad-collision PR body (the sibling PR's, verbatim) — root-caused and the lesson recorded; also the create-refusal message pinned, the schema constant belt-and-braces tested, the change log taught to report attribution replacement.
- **PR #101 (CLI, three rounds + rebase).** update --assign/--unassign/--force; exit 10 / category `assigned` (a refusal that provably never accompanies a write); next skipping tasks held only by others, --any, and next --claim as the one-stroke pick-and-claim; terminal board chips; agentdocs + SKILL.md teaching the real claim workflow, golden-pinned as machine contract. The review found the claim contract's documented outcomes were initially fiction — next --claim could never exit 10 (selection and gate now provably ask one question of one list, with the gate honestly reframed as a same-clone guarantee), the lost push race was never reported (now: the fetch that replays a claim emits assignment-shared, exactly once, from sync/fetch/next or — the round-3 gap — the ordinary take-it-up command that itself reconciles the shared task), and the skip stranded the spike's own claimants (now: both holders still offered the shared task; a second claim writes nothing). The core refactor (AssignMutation as a thin door onto UpdateMutation for one-pack composition) verified byte-identical across three revisions; the four-family composition (--status --comment --attach-url --assign self) is one commit, one pack.
- **PR #104 (web display, one round — the batch's only single-round APPROVE).** Assignee chips on board cards, server-side single-sourced through the same presentation functions the terminal prints (proven by mutating the Go rule and watching every render path follow with no client edit); 3-chip cap + "+N more" with the full list on the task page's read-only Assignments section (staleness matching the CLI to the second, following the poll without touching form state). Display-only by contract: assignment-shaped bodies refused before the service, pinned. Unheld cards 0.00px from main everywhere; held growth bounded; CSP byte-identical with zero blocked requests.

**Noted residuals (accepted):** a staleness-phrase rollover rebuilds the task-page section's rows (per-row signature is the fix if felt); standalone `workbook push` in a fresh process keeps pre-existing git-flavored rejection wording for races the sync path reports softly; signed-commit verification remains the opt-in future hardening for authenticated identity (deliberate, per design).
